categories.main_business_segments: Aoyama Trading Co., Ltd. operates through seven main business segments: Business Wear (men's and women's business apparel and accessories), Card (credit card services), Printing & Media (promotional and printing services), General Merchandise Sales (100-yen shops under the Daiso brand), Comprehensive Repair Services (shoe repair and key duplication under the Mister Minit brand), Franchisee Business (operating franchise restaurants, reuse shops, and fitness centers), and Real Estate (property management and leasing). The group also engages in web media and miscellaneous retail businesses.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages efficient retail operations, POS systems, and supply chain management for its apparel business, with manufacturing outsourced to subsidiaries and partners in China and Indonesia. It emphasizes sustainable materials, such as biodegradable fibers and water-saving dyeing technologies, and incorporates digital marketing, OMO (Online Merges with Offline), and DX (digital transformation) initiatives. The repair business utilizes standardized service processes and brand management for Mister Minit.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Aoyama Trading primarily serves general consumers in Japan seeking business and formal wear, as well as customers of 100-yen shops, repair services, and franchise restaurants/fitness centers. Its business wear segment targets working professionals, while other segments address broader retail and service needs. The company also provides B2B services through its printing and media segment, mainly to retail and distribution clients.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s core operations are concentrated in Japan, with an extensive nationwide retail network. It also has international operations, particularly in China (apparel manufacturing and retail), Indonesia (manufacturing), and the Asia-Pacific region (repair services in Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, and Malaysia). Over 90% of sales and assets are based in Japan.
categories.supply_chain_position: Aoyama Trading operates primarily at the downstream (retail and service) end of the supply chain, directly engaging with end consumers through its stores and service outlets. It also manages midstream activities such as apparel design, procurement, and logistics, with some upstream involvement via manufacturing subsidiaries and contracted factories.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus includes strengthening OMO and DX initiatives, optimizing inventory and store operations, expanding EC and digital marketing, and enhancing sustainability (ESG, CO2 reduction, responsible sourcing). It aims to maintain profitability in core stores, pursue new store formats, invest in human capital and diversity, and develop new businesses and M&A opportunities. There is no significant in-house R&D, but innovation is pursued through process improvement, digitalization, and sustainable product development.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through direct product sales (apparel, general merchandise), service fees (repair, franchise operations), credit card fees and interest, and property leasing. The company also earns from B2B printing/media services and franchise royalties. Revenue recognition is based on point-of-sale for goods and upon service delivery for repairs and franchise operations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Aoyama Trading is a leading player in Japan’s business wear retail market, facing competition from other major suit retailers (e.g., AOKI Holdings, Haruyama, Konaka), as well as from fast fashion and casual apparel brands due to the casualization of office wear. In other segments, it competes with large discount retailers, service chains, and franchise operators. The company is recognized for its scale, brand strength, and nationwide presence.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated sales were approximately 194.8 billion yen, with operating profit of 12.6 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent shareholders of 9.4 billion yen. The company has over 6,500 employees (including part-time), a strong balance sheet, and a stable, mature growth profile. Recent years have seen recovery from pandemic impacts, with moderate sales growth and improved profitability, and a mid-term plan targeting 210 billion yen in sales and 17 billion yen in operating profit by FY2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Aoyama Trading differentiates itself through its dominant retail network, comprehensive product lineup for business and formal wear, and strong brand recognition (notably 'Yofuku-no-Aoyama'). The company emphasizes customer service, value for money, and convenience, while increasingly focusing on digital integration (OMO), sustainability, and tailored offerings (e.g., custom order suits, functional materials). Its multi-business portfolio and commitment to ESG further enhance its competitive positioning.
